newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian silver falls further, gold steady.
newsitem.headline: Indian silver falls further, gold steady.

text.p: ** Silver (.999) falls further by 45 rupees to 6,795 rupees per kg on a weak world trend and in the absence of local demand. It lost 55 rupees per kg on Monday.
** Gold 24 carats remains steady at 4,680 rupees per kg, with traders reporting poor activity. Gold last gained 10 rupees per 10 grammes on Friday.
** Gold biscuits (116.50 grammes) also open unchanged at 54,800 rupees per piece.
Silver (.999) fell further by 45 rupees on Tuesday on a weak world trend, dealers said.
On Monday silver closed 55 rupees lower at 6,840 rupees per kg after making a feeble attempt at recovery in the absence of consumer and industrial demand.

Gold remained steady for the second day in a row at 4,680 rupees per 10 grammes in the absence of any activity. The price of a gold biscuit (116.50 grammes) was also unchanged at 54,800 rupees per piece.
"Imports of silver are coming into the country because of weak world prices. Locally, there's no support for silver," said a dealer.
Dealers attributed the lack of demand for both gold and silver to the slack period that sets in after the conclusion of the traditional wedding season in May. (Conversion $1=35.77 rupees)
